description: 文件系统操作（自 commands/filesystem.rs + search.rs 的 glob 拆出，kernel-plugin-runtime P2-2）

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List files and subdirectories in a directory (recursive up to 4 levels deep). Returns name, path, type (file/dir), and size for each entry.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to list

tools.name: list_directory_flat
tools.description: List the immediate files and subdirectories of a directory (non-recursive). Internal consumer tool (not model-facing).

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to list

tools.name: read_file_content
tools.description: Read the content of a file on disk. Returns text in cat -n format (6-digit line number + tab + content). Use offset and limit to read a specific range of lines (0-indexed). Use to inspect source code files when analyzing dependencies or investigating violations.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed, default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return (default: all lines)

tools.name: read_memory_batch
tools.description: Read multiple memory files under .lantai in one call. Internal consumer tool (not model-facing).

tools.name: read_file_base64
tools.description: Read a file and return its content base64-encoded (for in-app media rendering). Internal consumer tool (not model-facing).

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to read

tools.name: write_file_content
tools.description: Create or overwrite a file with the given content. Creates parent directories if needed. Use to write new files or modify existing ones.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to create or overwrite

_forceGate.description: Bypass the architecture gate for HIGH-risk writes. Set to true only after confirming safety via trace_impact.

tools.name: log_append
tools.description: Append content to a log file (create if missing). Internal consumer tool (not model-facing).

path.description: Absolute path to the log file

tools.name: create_directory
tools.description: Create a new directory (and any missing parent directories). Use before writing new files into a directory that may not exist yet.

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to create

tools.name: get_global_memory_dir
tools.description: Return the global memory directory path. Internal consumer tool (not model-facing).

tools.name: delete_file_or_dir
tools.description: Delete a file or directory at the specified path. Use to clean up temporary files or remove unwanted code. DANGEROUS — cannot be undone. Verify with user if deleting important files.

path.description: Absolute path to the file or directory to delete

_forceGate.description: Bypass the architecture gate for HIGH-risk writes. Set to true only after confirming safety via trace_impact.

tools.name: rename_file_or_dir
tools.description: Rename a file or directory (keep it in the same parent directory). For moving to a different directory, use move_file instead.

path.description: Absolute path to the file/directory to rename

new_name.description: New name (not path, just the name)

_forceGate.description: Bypass the architecture gate for HIGH-risk writes. Set to true only after confirming safety via trace_impact.

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file or directory. The destination path determines the new name/location.

_forceGate.description: Bypass the architecture gate for HIGH-risk writes. Set to true only after confirming safety via trace_impact.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching using glob patterns. Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time. Supports ** for recursive matching (e.g. "**/*.rs", "src/**/*.ts", "*.json"). Use this instead of run_shell to find files by name pattern — it is faster and respects .gitignore-style exclusions.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.rs", "src/**/agent*.ts", "*.json")

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the current workspace root.
